**Subject: Tuesday reading club – new attendance figures, and something I should flag**

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, because there has been a real change in the Tuesday reading club since your email of 30 October. I understood your reasons for proposing a pause from January: attendance had been low, and the increase in the hall insurance is another difficulty. I don’t pretend that better numbers solve every practical question, but I do hope you might reconsider the pause in light of where we are now.

The club has been running since September 2025, on Tuesdays from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library. We had five children most weeks in September, rising to nine by mid-October. Last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen. More than the numbers, there is now a lovely sense of the children settling in and beginning to belong.

Declan Moran of Salthill Book Nook has donated 120 books, mostly suitable for the 6–9 age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. They have made a great difference to the choice we can put out each week. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her little sister in English at the end of each session. Another boy, who would scarcely open a book in September, asked last week whether he could take two home with him. Those may sound like small things, but to anyone who has taught children they are exactly the moments that tell you something is taking root. It would be a terrible pity to pause the club just as it has taken off.

There is also something I need to tell you myself, before you hear it from anyone else. I met Orla Keane, a reporter with the *Corrib Courier*, at the farmers’ market. I got carried away telling her about the club and said she could “come along any Tuesday”. She would now like to visit on Tuesday 24 November and bring a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple. I know full well that photographs of children cannot be taken without your sign-off and the parental consent forms, and I should not have issued even a general invitation before speaking to you. I am not trying to present you with a done deal, and I have no wish to go around you.

I can ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you decide what, if anything, should happen. If you think the coverage would not be appropriate, I will explain that to her. If you are open to it after the review, I would be very willing to collect the consent forms myself and help with whatever arrangements you require. Nothing would go ahead without your approval. Thoughtful local coverage could be wonderful for the club and might help us attract more children, books or support, but only if it is done properly and under your direction.

I hope this gives you a fuller picture before the 18th. Would you be willing to look again at the proposed January pause, including the attendance figures, so that we can discuss at the review whether there is a workable way forward? I would be glad to help in any way I can with the insurance question or other practicalities.

With best wishes,

[Your name]
